## Technical Corrections to This Historical Draft

This source is retained for audit history and is excluded from the production reading path. The corrections below govern its interpretation; the original wording is preserved separately.

For a declared constant-mass system in an inertial frame, total external force satisfies $\dot p=F_{\rm ext}$, so its time integral equals the total momentum change. Internal force pairs cancel from that system's total momentum balance. This is Newtonian momentum balance, not a consequence of taking an infinitesimal-perturbation limit.

Actual power is evaluated on the actual velocity: for particles, $\dot T=\sum_i F_i\cdot v_i$ when all force powers are included. If conservative potential is included in the energy, its power must not be counted again as an external contribution. Virtual work pairs force with an admissible virtual displacement at a fixed time; it is not generally actual work accumulated along a trajectory.

Force and power ledgers add on one specified motion. Changing a force changes that motion, so separately simulated finite outcomes need not add. See [same-state and forward comparisons](../../../appendix-applications.html).

::: {.callout-warning collapse="true" title="Historical Draft: Superseded Wording"}

## 1. Impulse and Momentum

Forces integrate to momentum change. This is an exact consequence of
infinitesimal superposition.

## 2. Work and Energy

Power integrates to energy change. Virtual work accumulates linearly
along nonlinear trajectories.

## 3. Sensitivity and Influence

Integrated variations quantify sensitivity of final state to
infinitesimal causes, not fractional causation.

:::
